## Content Board Curator

**Daily 12:15.** The homelab's GitHub board keeps the ideas: open issues labelled `post` on `datahub-local/datahub-local`. This workflow is the read-only bridge from that board into the blog lane's `article_queue`, plus the queue's own age ceiling.

**Import.** Each labelled issue becomes one `article_queue` row: `ENTRY_ID` `gh-<number>`, the issue title as `TOPIC`, the body as `DESCRIPTION`, the issue URL as `LINK`, and the defaults from `datasets/board_intake.json` for `CATEGORIES` / `ASSET_TYPES` / `MAX_WORDS` / `PRIORITY`, `ORIGIN=BOARD`, `STATUS=QUEUE`. An issue already in the queue (by `ENTRY_ID` or `LINK`) is skipped, so the board is never written to and an issue stays open until a human closes it.

**Ceiling.** Any `article_queue` row still QUEUE, IN_PROGRESS or WAITING_APPROVAL whose last update is older than `cancel_after_days` (from `datasets/curator_config.json`, the same value Content Feed Curator uses) is set CANCELLED - a stuck run or an unanswered approval, not a live one, because the clock is the row's own UPDATE_DATE.

**Env vars:** none beyond the two credentials. The board is public, so the GitHub read needs no special scope.

nodes.name: schedule_trigger
nodes.notes: Daily 12:15. Fifteen minutes after Content Feed Curator, so the two writes to content_planner never overlap; the exact minute is not load-bearing, the article lane drains on its own schedule.

nodes.name: list_board_issues
nodes.notes: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues?labels=<label>&state=<state>. alwaysOutputData: an empty board (or no labelled issue) must not stop the run, or the queue's own ceiling would never run on a quiet week. Read-only - the workflow never comments on, labels or closes an issue.

nodes.name: read_article_queue
nodes.notes: The dedupe source and the ceiling's input, read once at the top. alwaysOutputData: an empty queue is a normal first run, and the intake still has to append to it.

nodes.name: append_article_queue
nodes.notes: Appends only the columns the row owns; every lifecycle column is written blank so the article lane starts the row from a known state. ENTRY_ID is the issue number, which is what makes the next run's dedupe exact.

nodes.name: cancel_stale_articles
nodes.notes: Both fields: STATUS=CANCELLED takes the row out of the article lane's QUEUE, ARTICLE_STATUS=CANCELLED stops pick_candidate resuming a claimed row that never finished. This lane spells it with two L's.

nodes.name: click_trigger
nodes.notes: The schedule runs it daily; this lets the editor's Execute workflow force one on demand, the same pair Content Feed Curator carries.
